and dissertations all in .pdf format. Using a pdf to text converter, I
ended up converting each of the files one bye one. This solution is
probably very elementary, though, and it'd be great to learn how to do

converted the files to txt, the footnotes got in the middle of the
main text, which means I lose a lot of data when looking for
concordances and contexts.

I still don't know how to solve this problem, so for now I'm using the
corpus despite of the "footnote interruptions"...

messages.subject: Question about Dist {amap} vectorsize
messages.body_plain:
Dear all, I have a question about distance matrix computation (Dist in package amap).
I have a relatively large dataframe (a) with about 2,000,000 observations of 3 variables (1 categorical factor with 10 levels, 1 categorical factor with about 40000 levels, and a numerical factor with 10 levels).
After converting it into a table (b<-table(a$Fac1, a$Fac2, a$Fac§)) this table has about 4,000,000 entries. If I try to do a distance computation with Dist (c<-Dist(b, method="correlation", upper=T, diag=T) I get an error message telling me that the vector size is too large (Error in double(N*(N-1)/2)).
Is there a maximal size for vectors and if so what is this size. If I knew this I might be able to try for a smaller sample, although I would like to use the whole data. Can anyone help me with that, or am I just making some stupid beginner's mistake?
Thanks a lot,
Marco

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Question about Dist {amap} vectorsize
messages.subject_clean: [CorpLing with R] Question about Dist {amap} vectorsize
messages.body_plain:
I think part of the problem might be because you're using a table. Look here:

library(amap)
x <- rnorm(2000000)
y <- rnorm(2000000)
z <- rnorm(2000000)

xyz <- rbind(x,y,z)

system.time(Dist(as.table(xyz)))
   user  system elapsed
  4.540   0.050   4.572
system.time(Dist(xyz))
   user  system elapsed
  0.100   0.000   0.068

Dist on a table takes MUCH MUCH longer than Dist on a matrix.

What I ended up doing on a similar occasion was write a script that
did the computation of similarity measures one by one separately. That
is, my script generated a matrix of NA, looped over all combinations
of rows and columns, computed sim_i,j, and inserted the measure into
the matrix at i,j and j,i. That whole thing got outsourced into a
dedicated linux server (at the MPI). It took 5 days (because I had
several 100K measures to do) but it worked.

STG
--
Stefan Th. Gries
-----------------------------------------------
University of California, Santa Barbara
http://www.linguistics.ucsb.edu/faculty/stgries
-----------------------------------------------

Which test is appropriate for differences between TTRs?

Best

messages.subject: Re: Load PDF into R
messages.body_plain:
Fernanda, your question made me think about how I might go about
trying to preserve the file names on concordance results after
converting files from PDF to text. Here's what I wrote in answer to
that question. (Excuse the overload on detail, but that's how I write
my scripts.) Best of luck. Earl Brown

############################
# this section converts PDF to text and then loads each text file into
R and search them

rm(list=ls(all=T))

# loads the function exact matches
source(file="/Users/brow2662/Documents/_qclwr/fn_em2.r")

# gets the file names with a .pdf extension
file.names<-dir("/Users/brow2662/Documents/test_pdf_conversion",
pattern=".pdf$", full.names=T)

# creates a collector for all results
all.results<-character()

# defines search.term
search.term<-"\\bfrequency\\b"

# loop to convert PDF to text and then search for search.term
for (i in file.names) {

	# progress report
	cat("Working on ", basename(i), "\n", sep="")

	# gets current file name
	current.file.name <http://current.file.name><-basename(i)
	current.file.name <http://current.file.name><-sub("\\.pdf", "", current.file.name <http://current.file.name>,
ignore.case=T, perl=T)

	# sets the three arguments for the call to system()
	function.location<-"/usr/local/bin/pdftotext"
	input.file<-paste("'", i, "'", sep="")
	output.file<-paste("/Users/brow2662/Documents/test_pdf_conversion/",
current.file.name <http://current.file.name>, ".txt", sep="")

	# converts current PDF to text
	system(paste(function.location, input.file, output.file, sep=" "))

	# creates the pathway to the newly created text file
	current.file.text.name <http://current.file.text.name><-sub(".pdf$", ".txt", i, ignore.case=T,
perl=T)

	# loads the newly created text file into R and converts it to unicode
	current.file<-scan(file=current.file.text.name <http://current.file.text.name>, what="char",
sep="\n", quote="", comment.char="", quiet=T)
	current.file<-iconv(current.file, "LATIN1", "UTF-8")

	# searches the current text for search.term and gets the context
delimited matches
	current.results<-exact.matches(search.term, current.file, pcre=T,
case.sens=F, characters.around=50)[[4]]

	# if no hits in current file, goes to next file
	if (length(current.results)==0) {
		next
	}

	# adds the current file name before the results
	current.results<-paste(current.file.name <http://current.file.name>, current.results, sep="\t")

	# adds current results to all results
	all.results<-append(all.results, current.results)

} # next file

# saves all results to hard drive
cat("FILE\tPRE\tHIT\tFOL", all.results, file="/Users/brow2662/
Documents/test_pdf_conversion/results_search.txt", sep="\n")

# announces finish
cat("\aAll done!\n")

############################
